content.text: Setting up a sovereign digital store is a four-step sequence that most creators overcomplicate by [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-start-selling-digital-products-crypto-step-step-12|COREMERCH guide to start]]ing in the wrong order. Step one is the backend: Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script handles payment verification, order logging, and product delivery. Step two is the payment layer: NOWPayments connects your wallet addresses to the checkout flow — no KYC required from you or your buyer. Step three is the storefront: Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages serves your store for free with no server management. Step four is testing: [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/complete-deep-dive-digital-product-stores-kyc-payments-5|The Complete]] a real mainnet transaction, confirm the webhook fires, the order logs, and the delivery email arrives with a working download link. Only after step four passes cleanly should you promote the store. COREMERCH deploys the complete Edge Stack — Cloudflare Pages plus Workers plus [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-supabase-order-database-digital-stores-works-how-18|supabase]] plus NOWPayments — in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The sovereign commerce infrastructure is built on the principles of ownership and decentralization, allowing creators to have full control over their digital stores. By leveraging platforms like Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, and NOWPayments, creators can establish a robust and scalable infrastructure that is not dependent on traditional payment platforms. This approach ensures that creators can continue to operate their stores even if traditional platforms experience downtime or impose restrictions.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying a digital store on Cloudflare Pages, creators need to prepare several key components. These include a domain name, a GitHub or Cloudflare account, and a NOWPayments account for crypto payment processing. Additionally, creators should have a clear understanding of their product offerings, pricing, and target audience. With these elements in place, creators can proceed to set up their store's infrastructure, ensuring a seamless and efficient deployment process.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Setting up a payment and delivery pipeline is a critical step in deploying a digital store. Creators can utilize NOWPayments to facilitate crypto transactions, eliminating the need for traditional payment platforms. By integrating NOWPayments with their store, creators can enable automatic payment verification and instant product delivery. This streamlined process enhances the overall customer experience, fostering trust and loyalty among customers.
Deploy your digital store on Cloudflare Pages for free.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once the infrastructure is set up, creators can go live with their digital store and start processing transactions. The first transaction is a significant milestone, as it validates the store's functionality and payment pipeline. Creators can test their store's performance by simulating transactions or offering free products to gauge customer response. By closely monitoring their store's performance, creators can identify areas for improvement and optimize their infrastructure for enhanced efficiency and scalability.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The post-deployment ownership transfer is explicit in every COREMERCH deployment. When the build is complete and the end-to-end test passes, COREMERCH provides the credentials and configuration details for every component under the customer's accounts. The GitHub or Cloudflare repository is under the customer's account from the start. The Supabase or Google Sheets database is under the customer's account. The NOWPayments account is under the customer's email. COREMERCH removes collaborator access upon delivery. From that point, the store runs entirely under the customer's own accounts.
How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?

The setup sequence matters because each component depends on the previous one being correctly configured. Start with NOWPayments: create your account, configure wallet addresses for each coin you want to accept, generate the API key, and note the IPN secret key you will set. Then configure the backend: in Stack 01, deploy the Google Apps Script Web App and note its URL; in Stack 02, deploy the Cloudflare Worker and note its URL. Set that URL as the webhook endpoint in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Then configure the storefront. Then run a real mainnet test — send actual crypto to your configured wallet address, confirm NOWPayments detects it, confirm the webhook fires, and confirm the delivery email arrives with a working download link.
Leverage NOWPayments for crypto payment processing.
Related: How Creators Like You Are Building Sovereign Stores

Creators at the store setup stage comparing Stack 01 and Stack 02 are typically choosing between building it themselves with the Sovereign Blueprint at $47 — which covers both stacks in complete detail with full source code — or having COREMERCH deploy the complete Edge Stack under their accounts with the Edge Commerce Stack at $197. Both result in the same ownership structure: your GitHub or Cloudflare account, your Supabase database, your NOWPayments account, your wallet, your store. See both options at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Follow the setup sequence without skipping steps — configuration errors are significantly harder to diagnose than setup time. First: create your NOWPayments account, add wallet addresses, generate your API key, and note your IPN secret key. Second: deploy the backend — configure Cloudflare Worker with your NOWPayments credentials and product settings, or configure Google Apps Script with the same — and confirm the endpoint URL. Third: set the webhook endpoint URL in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Fourth: deploy the storefront to Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages and confirm product pages and checkout display correctly. Fifth: configure your custom domain and DNS if using one. Sixth: complete a real mainnet test transaction. Seventh: check the order database for the test entry. Only after steps six and seven pass cleanly should you share the store URL publicly.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the cost of deploying a digital store on Cloudflare Pages?
Cloudflare Pages offers a free plan, making it an attractive option for creators.
Do I need to have coding skills to deploy a digital store?
While coding skills can be beneficial, they are not required to deploy a digital store on Cloudflare Pages.
How do I handle customer support for my digital store?
You can handle customer support through email or by integrating a support platform into your store.
Can I use traditional payment platforms with my digital store?
While possible, using traditional payment platforms may restrict your store's scalability and flexibility.
How do I optimize my digital store's performance for high traffic volumes?
You can optimize your store's performance by leveraging Cloudflare Pages' scalability features and exploring edge computing solutions.
